Actual: Revora uses affected @auth/core 0.41.2 and next-auth beta.31 with the email provider and no normalizeIdentifier override. The default validates one ASCII @ before Unicode normalization and auth.ts passes the result unchanged to Resend. GitHub's reviewed advisory classifies this configuration as potential no-interaction account takeover when the downstream mail path normalizes a homoglyph separator; patched versions are @auth/core 0.41.3 / next-auth beta.32
Root cause: A newly published upstream vulnerability is directly reachable through Revora's only production sign-in method and no application-level canonicalization/rejection mitigates it
User/business risk: An attacker who knows a user's email may be able to redirect a passwordless sign-in link to an attacker-controlled mailbox and obtain that user's account health history subscription and data-right actions
Fix: Upgrade to the patched Auth.js release or canonicalize NFKC then validate exactly one ASCII @ before Auth.js and before delivery; invalidate outstanding verification tokens after remediation
Regression test: Unicode separator corpus through sign-in request and delivery-recipient seam asserting rejection plus authenticated cross-account denial
Retest: R012 and R013 fail; source reachability confirmed. The getToken advisory is not reachable because Revora never calls getToken and the OAuth mix-up advisory is not reachable because only one email provider is configured. No exploit email was sent and no fix is authorized
Validation evidence: package-lock: @auth/core 0.41.2 + next-auth 5.0.0-beta.31 (affected); npm audit --omit=dev exits 1 listing GHSA-7rqj-j65f-68wh (critical); installed node_modules/@auth/core/lib/actions/signin/send-token.js:74-98 defaultNormalizer splits on ASCII @ with no Unicode normalization; auth.ts Resend provider sets no normalizeIdentifier and passes params.identifier unchanged to sendEmail. getToken advisory unreachable (grep: zero first-party getToken calls); OAuth advisory unreachable (email provider only). Patched @auth/core 0.41.3 / next-auth 5.0.0-beta.32 exist on npm.
Root cause group: G4 auth dependency and identity chain

Surface: Guest check-page console and network hygiene
Reproduction: Open /check?stay=1 in a fresh anonymous Mobile Chrome context then submit a deterministic clinical case while recording every >=400 response console warning page error and failed request
Expected: The supported no-login core journey has no relevant console or network errors
Actual: GET /api/history returns 401 on every fresh guest check page and Chromium logs Failed to load resource as an error; the visible flow still completes. The 237-case Playwright suite does not fail on console/network output
Root cause: CheckPage always mounts DailyLoop; DailyLoop calls loadHistory and loadHistory attempts the authenticated remote history endpoint before it falls back to on-device history without first knowing the user is signed out
User/business risk: Routine unauthorized traffic adds noise to browser diagnostics and monitoring and can conceal a real 401 regression; it also violates the stated clean-console completion gate
Fix: Avoid the remote history request for a known guest or make the guest history endpoint return an intentional non-error empty contract while preserving authorization on private data

Root cause group: G3 provider coupling and failure-path semantics
